topic: What if you could shrink anything? (60 s Short, vertical)
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SHRINK ANYTHING?
style: NIGHT PRINT world (sets in two inks, pink power) with the Ink Stick cast (the house look, final). Also built in Cel 3D, Paper Fold, Plush and Painted 2D. 1080 x 1920 for YouTube Shorts.

power.rule: anything you point at, down to any size; it gets smaller, never lighter
power.look: pink caliper jaws clamp the thing on a ruler, the readout counts down, the thing squeezes down with pink ghost trails and keeps a pink edge

script.text: Too much to pack? Shrink. It all fits.

script.beat: 1 cold open, demo 2 (useful, the first hint of the cost)
script.text: Couch stuck on the stairs? Shrink. Still heavy.
Annoying little sister? Shrink. Uh oh.
What if you could shrink anything?
Homework mountain? Shrink. A whole pizza? Shrink. One bite. Still every calorie.

script.beat: 4 the not-so-fun part: the rule and the real science
script.text: Because here's the catch: things get smaller, never lighter. Shrink something to a twentieth of its size, and it's eight thousand times denser. Shrink the Earth to sixteen millimetres, a marble, and it's a black hole. That's real.
And that toy couch? Still forty kilos. The floor gives way.
Next morning, a man in a suit knocks at your door. He's seen the hole in the floor. He knows what you can do. And he wants you to shrink something for him. Something big.

script.beat: 6 a choice with family at stake
script.text: Then he looks at your sister, still mouse-sized. 'Our lab can make her big again,' he says. 'If you help us.'
What would you do? Part one.

science.claim: Shrink something to a twentieth of its size, and it's eight thousand times denser.
science.working: Under the rule (smaller, never lighter) the mass stays the same while every length is scaled by 1/20, so the volume is scaled by (1/20)^3 = 1/8000. Density = mass / volume, so it goes up 8,000 times.
science.source: Density = mass / volume; volume scales with the cube of length

science.claim: Shrink the Earth to sixteen millimetres (a marble) and it's a black hole.
science.working: A mass becomes a black hole once it fits inside its Schwarzschild radius, r = 2GM/c^2. For Earth: 2 x 6.674e-11 x 5.972e24 / (2.998e8)^2 = 8.87e-3 m, a radius of 8.87 mm (17.7 mm across). A standard 16 mm marble (radius 8 mm) is inside that, so all of Earth's mass in a 16 mm ball is a black hole.
science.source: Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c^2; Earth's mass 5.972e24 kg (NASA Earth Fact Sheet); G and c from CODATA 2018; standard marble 5/8 inch (16 mm)

science.claim: A shrunk pizza still has every calorie.
science.working: The power's rule keeps all the matter, and the energy in food is in its matter (its chemical bonds), so the bite holds all the pizza's calories. No number is stated on screen.
science.source: The episode's rule; food energy is chemical energy stored in the food's mass

science.claim: The toy couch is still forty kilos.
science.working: Story fact, not science: the couch is set at 40 kg (a light two-seat couch), the same as in the 20 s cut.
